summary: Regional-affinity shift causes auth retries and P99 latency spike crossing EU/US boundary
description: Issue summary: Customer (NovaHealth Labs, enterprise) reports repeated authorization retries and a sustained p99 latency increase (~800ms -> 1.9s) for inference calls originating from EU clients. The symptom started after a routine routing config churn during a low-traffic maintenance window. Impact: several production user-facing endpoints experienced timeouts and auth failures for ~27 minutes, causing degraded UX and retried billing. Timeline: 2026-03-12 03:05 UTC first alerts (p99 > 1.0s), 03:12 UTC customer report, 03:18 UTC automated autoscaler activity observed, 03:25 UTC partial mitigation applied, 03:32 UTC traffic normalizing but auth retries observed through 03:40 UTC. Observed behavior: requests from eu-west-1 intermittently routed to a us-east-1 pool that had a different model variant pinned by fallbacks. When route hop occurred, the customer's token exchange to our auth proxy failed transiently (401 followed by 429), triggering client-side retries and higher end-to-end latency. No errors reported for traffic originating from us-east-1. Customer impact: session timeouts in NovaHealth's clinician UI and multiple help-desk tickets. Additional notes: customer is on enterprise plan and uses strict region preference headers in their integration.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a client with region header set to eu-west and enterprise account token for NovaHealth Labs
2) Send sustained burst of inference requests (40rps) to /v1/generate for gpt-redwood-13b-quantized
3) Observe routing decisions in request trace IDs returned in headers (x-rw-route, x-rw-region)
4) Watch for intermittent x-rw-region showing us-east-1 and corresponding 401/429 auth events in access logs

comments: 2026-03-12 03:20 - Aisha Khan (Support): Logged initial customer report and escalated to SRE. Noted correlation with routing churn during maintenance window. Asked customer for example trace IDs.

2026-03-12 03:28 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Confirmed intermittent route handoff to us-east-1. Observed that fallback routing selected a model variant not available in eu-west pool, triggering cross-region rehome. Hypothesis: routing policy TTL mismatch + variant availability caused rehoming.
2026-03-12 03:30 - NovaHealth Support Rep (Customer): Provided traces and confirmed clinician UI timeouts. Customer requested immediate pin to eu-west while we investigate.

2026-03-12 03:34 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Applied temporary routing override to enforce strict regional affinity for NovaHealth (api key scoped). Monitoring for reduction in auth retries and p99. Noted reduction in p99 to ~900ms within 6 minutes.

2026-03-12 04:00 - Sophie Leclerc (Platform): Will follow up with permanent fix proposal: sync routing TTL and expand eu-west pool model variants. Opening INT-9921 to coordinate capacity and deployment of quantized model in eu-west.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between admin-triggered routing config refresh (2026-03-12 02:58 UTC) and onset of affinity shifts.
Routing decision logs show fallback to 'compatible-variant' rule when exact model variant not present in preferred region.
Auth proxy validates audience against token binding to origin region; cross-region handoff caused token-mismatch condition for a subset of requests where token binding TTL had expired.

Autoscaler brought additional capacity in us-east which briefly accepted the cross-region traffic; that pool used a different quantization profile (slower cold-starts for first chunk) increasing observed latency.
No degradation found in network fabric or DNS for eu-west; problem reproduced by forcing variant mismatch in staging routing rules.
root_cause: Routing policy allowed 'compatible-variant' fallthrough when exact pinned variant was temporarily unavailable in eu-west. Combined with a short token-binding TTL on the auth proxy, this produced transient 401s when routes rehomed to us-east. Also eu-west missing quantized model variant increased cold-starts which amplified p99.
resolution: Short term (mitigation): Applied per-customer strict regional affinity override for NovaHealth via routing API (no cross-region fallthrough). This returned p99 to acceptable range and stopped auth retries.
Medium term: Scheduled INT-9921 to deploy the missing quantized model variant to eu-west pool and to harmonize routing policy TTLs across control plane and auth proxy.

Long term: Add a preflight check during routing config refresh to prevent temporary variant gaps and implement a safer token-binding grace period for cross-region OTPs. Update runbook with a checklist for rolling routing changes to avoid this class of regressions.
Customer communication: Sent status update and recommended temporary client-side retry backoff changes. Customer accepted pin workaround and requested postmortem.
follow_up_actions: INT-9921: Deploy quantized gpt-redwood-13b variant to eu-west (owner: Sophie Leclerc)
PLT-2107: Add routing config refresh preflight to control plane (owner: Marco Ruiz)
DOC-404: Update customer-facing docs to explain region-affinity overrides and recommended token-binding settings for enterprise customers (owner: Product)
